title: Register the documented shared ranking CLI controls (--context-profile, --no-tools, --top, ...)
description:
README and the P4 contract document shared ranking controls that `sr rank` rejects as invalid usage: --context-profile standard|minimal, --no-tools, --messages N, --budget-chars N, --top K, --shortlist M, --gate X, --fits X and --timeout-ms N. For example, README's own example `sr rank --context scratch/context.json --context-profile minimal --dry-run` fails. The config keys and SR_* variables already exist in the key registry (docs/config-contract.md), with CLI precedence and restrict-only rules for the disclosure keys. The CLI layer just never registers these flags.

Scope: add the flags with strict clap parsing and the documented bounds, feeding the existing ConfigSources CLI layer so precedence and restrict-only disclosure rules apply unchanged. Add them to the capabilities registry.

Tests (real binary): each flag changes the effective value (doctor --config provenance, or dry-run request bytes). Out-of-bounds values are rejected as invalid-usage (2). A project config cannot widen a CLI minimal profile, while a CLI flag can narrow a trusted standard profile.

Found by CopperWren while implementing 5.15, whose README dry-run example depends on --context-profile.

title: Observing one session under two agent branches fails, and the constraint violation is reported as database corruption
description:
FOUND 2026-09-21 (RoseCoyote) by running the installed binary, while checking the identity fields around
sr-an94's new upgrade clause. Two defects, one user-visible failure.

REPRODUCTION, exactly as run.
  sr observe --transcript <t> --harness claude_code --branch main       --dir <L> --json  -> ok, 1 row
  sr observe --transcript <t> --harness claude_code --branch feature-x  --dir <L> --json  -> FAILS

The second exits 9 with:
  {"decision":"unavailable","error":{"code":9,"kind":"storage-failure",
    "message":"Failed to record observations: cache database could not be read safely",
    "hint":"Use sr --help; inspect trusted-user and project configuration.","retryable":false}}

Nothing is corrupt. The database is fine, and the row from the first branch is still there and readable.

DEFECT 1: the observation's primary key omits the branch that its uniqueness key includes.
  observation_id  = "obs-{session}-{event_id}-{skill_id}"                        (src/cli.rs)
  source_event_key = "{native|normalized}:{session}:{branch}:{event_id}:{skill_id}"
observation_id is the PRIMARY KEY of observations; source_event_key is UNIQUE. So a second branch produces
a DIFFERENT source_event_key and an IDENTICAL observation_id, and the insert dies on the primary key.
Confirmed directly against the same file:
  sqlite3: IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed: observations.observation_id

The same collision applies across producer namespaces: native and normalized observations of the same
session/event/skill differ in source_event_key's first segment only, so their observation_ids collide too.
AGENTS.md requires precisely the opposite: "Never merge those producer namespaces by path/ID", and
"Normalized imports cannot update native session state by repeating its IDs". Today they do not merge --
they make the second write fail.

This also matters because agent branch is a first-class identity in this product: AGENTS.md rule 1 is
"Bind state to workspace, session, and agent branch", `observe` documents `--branch NAME`, and the ledger
stores agent_branch on the row. A subagent or branch-scoped observation is therefore impossible to record
for a session another branch already observed.

FIX. Put the same identity in the primary key that the uniqueness key carries: the producer namespace and
the branch. Note the interaction with the clause landed for sr-an94 in 9aae0b6, which requires
`observations.observation_id = excluded.observation_id` before upgrading an attempt; a branch-aware id
keeps that check correct, and in fact makes it stricter.

DEFECT 2, which is what made the first one undiagnosable: EVERY unmapped SQLite error is reported as
corruption. src/storage/mod.rs:
    match error.sqlite_error_code() {
        ... Some(ErrorCode::SchemaChanged) => Self::IncompatibleSchema,
        _ => Self::Corrupt,          // <- ConstraintViolation lands here
    }
so a constraint violation -- an ordinary, expected outcome of a uniqueness rule -- is presented to a user
as "cache database could not be read safely", with a hint pointing at configuration. A person reading that
has every reason to believe their ledger is damaged, and the honest answer is that a row already existed.
StoreError already has better-fitting variants: InvalidRecord and RecordConflict.

Map ErrorCode::ConstraintViolation to a constraint-specific StoreError, keep Corrupt for actual corruption
(NotADatabase, Corrupt), and leave the catch-all as something neutral rather than an accusation.

TESTS REQUIRED.
- Two observes of one session under different --branch values both succeed and produce TWO rows, each
  carrying its own agent_branch. This fails today and is the planted negative.
- The same for native versus normalized ingestion of one session: two rows, no collision, no merge.
- A genuine uniqueness conflict is reported as a conflict, not as corruption: assert on the error kind and
  the message, not only on the exit code.
- An actually corrupt database still reports corruption, so the remapping does not hide the real thing.

RELATIONSHIP. Found while verifying sr-an94 (9aae0b6), which is correct and unaffected. Distinct from
sr-jgez, which is about the read window never advancing; this is about the write key. Both surfaced from
the same place: the observation path's identity handling.
close_reason: Independently verified (FuchsiaCave, not the author) at origin/main f41f133: f8182c0 is an ancestor. title: Resolve judgment skill identity to the stable skill ID, not the invocation name
notes:
REALITY CHECK 2026-09-21 (MagentaSquirrel). Found by driving the whole documented P5 journey against the
project's own TLS fixture at origin/main 16743e9, then reading the resulting ledger rows directly.

OBSERVED. `sr feedback EVENT --skill rust-code-review --verdict useful` stored the string
'rust-code-review' in judgments.skill_id, while ranking_candidates.skill_id for the very same skill
holds the stable opaque id 's_6d9c784e05bfd6ba44239ad4ca8c9695e8e0fe470aea70f310799aa02b14ce42'.
The event's roster_snapshots.members_json already carries the mapping, so the resolution was
available and simply was not performed.

    judgments:          ('jdg-7fda...', 'rc-sess-alpha-2', 'rust-code-review', 'useful')
    ranking_candidates: ('s_6d9c784e05bfd6ba...', 'wide'), ('s_6d9c784e05bfd6ba...', 'rerank')
    observations:       ('s_6d9c784e05bfd6ba...', 'attempted', 'rc-sess-alpha-2')

Note that OBSERVATIONS use the stable id correctly. The judgment write is the sole outlier, which
is what makes this a narrow fix rather than a schema question.

WHY IT MATTERS, in order of consequence.
1. `sr stats --by-skill` splits one skill across two rows: one keyed by the opaque id carrying
   top1_recommendations=1, and one keyed by 'rust-code-review' carrying judged_useful=1. Observed
   output: [('s_6d9c784e05bfd6ba44', 1, 0, 0), ('s_7f19075b2ab90d381b', 0, 0, 0),
   ('s_b9fe5e81e88f61b767', 0, 0, 0), ('rust-code-review', 0, 0, 1)]. Per-skill usefulness can
   therefore never be joined to per-skill recommendation volume, which is the entire point of
   --by-skill. A reader cannot see that the skill recommended once is the skill judged useful once.
2. Learned priors are specified as 'keyed by skill revision and policy context' (AGENTS.md). A prior
   keyed by an invocation name cannot join a candidate keyed by a stable id, so P8 priors would
   silently find no history. Fixing this before priors are built is much cheaper than after.
3. It violates an explicit AGENTS.md invariant: 'Separate identities. Keep stable opaque skill ID,
   actual invocation name, sanitized display name, source, content hash, and local load target
   distinct.' README also promises the judgment records 'a particular event and skill version'; a
   bare name is neither version-bound nor collision-free.
4. Invocation names are not unique across sources. AGENTS.md requires same-name skills to remain
   distinct where the harness permits, so two different skills sharing a name would collapse into
   one judgment key, and a renamed skill would orphan its own labels.

WHAT TO DO. Resolve the --skill argument against the event's retained roster snapshot at feedback
time and store the stable id, exactly as the observation path already does. Accept the invocation
name as the user-facing input, because that is what a human reads in the ranking output; the
resolution belongs inside the command, not in the caller. Preserve the existing typed refusals:
sr-roadmap-l1i.6.26 already requires that a missing or incomplete snapshot yield 'unknown
membership, not absence', and this must not weaken that. `feedback --instead` already refuses with
exit 10 'Roster snapshot missing or incomplete for event' when membership is unavailable; a
--verdict write should reach the same bar rather than falling back to an unresolved string.

MIGRATION. Existing judgment rows written with a name are ambiguous and must not be silently
rewritten: resolve them only where the retained snapshot proves a unique mapping, and leave the
rest identifiable as unresolved rather than guessing. Do not delete them.

TESTS REQUIRED.
- A judgment written by invocation name is stored under the stable skill id, verified by reading the
  row, not by reading the command's own output.
- --by-skill shows ONE row for a skill that was both recommended and judged, with both counts on it.
  This is the planted negative for the defect: with the fix reverted the row count is two.
- A name that resolves to two skills in the snapshot is refused rather than stored ambiguously.
- A judgment for an event whose snapshot is missing keeps sr-roadmap-l1i.6.26's unknown-membership
  behavior and does not write an unresolved name.
- Existing name-keyed rows survive a fix without being rewritten on a guess.

RELATIONSHIP TO EXISTING WORK. sr-roadmap-l1i.6.13 owns the report surface and sr-roadmap-l1i.6.26
owns the feedback and observation lifecycle. Neither names this identity resolution, which is why
this is tracked separately rather than assumed covered. It is a defect in the write path, not a
reporting preference.

REFINEMENT 1. Two things the first pass left unspecified.
(a) `feedback --instead ORIGINAL --skill X` writes TWO labels in one atomic transaction (original
    unsuitable, alternative useful). BOTH skill references need stable-id resolution, not just the
    --verdict one, and the atomicity must hold across the resolution: a resolvable original with an
    unresolvable alternative must write neither label, since AGENTS.md requires that 'a failed alternate
    lookup cannot leave an unintended standalone negative label'.
(b) The judgments table may carry a uniqueness or foreign-key constraint keyed on skill_id; check the
    DDL before changing what is written, and state in the fix whether existing name-keyed rows can
    coexist with id-keyed rows under that constraint. If they cannot, the migration is not optional and
    belongs in the ledger's versioned migration path rather than in an ad-hoc rewrite.
Test to add for (a): a --instead whose alternative cannot be resolved leaves zero new judgment rows,
verified by reading the table, not by the command's exit code.

REFINEMENT 2. Do not DISCARD the invocation name when resolving; store both.

The first pass said 'store the stable id', which would lose evidence. The name the assessor supplied is
provenance: it records what a human actually typed, and AGENTS.md requires the stable id, the invocation
name and the display name to be kept DISTINCT rather than collapsed into one another. Replacing one with
the other is the same category of mistake in the opposite direction.

So the judgment row should carry the resolved stable skill_id as its join key AND the supplied
invocation name as recorded provenance, exactly as the ranking output already carries both for a
candidate. That also makes the migration tractable: an existing name-keyed row can be resolved forward
while keeping the original string visible, so nothing is rewritten on a guess and an unresolvable row
stays legible as unresolved.

REFINEMENT 3, cross-bead. sr-oufi and sr-an94 both feed the same user-visible surface and neither alone
proves it coherent. Add ONE joint end-to-end case, owned by whichever lands second, that runs the whole
documented loop in the order a user would: rank against a real provider, observe the tool_use in one pass
and its result in a LATER pass, record a judgment by invocation name, then `stats --json --by-skill`.
Required result: exactly ONE row for that skill carrying top1_recommendations=1, observed_loads=1 and
judged_useful=1 together.

Today that assertion fails twice over -- two rows, and the load counted as attempted -- so it is the
planted negative for both beads at once. Neither bead's own tests establish it, because each fixes one
half of one row.

Every AC maps to a real-SQLite test that passed in my full local run (load 168->123): stored under the stable id, read from the row (a_judgment_supplied_by_invocation_name_is_stored_under_the_stable_skill_id); one --by-skill row (a_skill_recommended_and_judged_by_name_reports_one_by_skill_row); ambiguous name refused (an_invocation_name_matching_two_skills_is_refused_rather_than_guessed); missing snapshot refused without a write (a_name_with_no_match_and_no_snapshot_is_refused_without_writing, plus 0090ee4 refusing name lookups against partial snapshots); legacy name rows untouched (a_judgment_already_stored_under_a_name_is_left_untouched). R1(a): record_paired_correction resolves both references inside one transaction before any write (ineligible_alternative_aborts_transaction_zero_judgments; an unresolvable alternative becomes a prospective proposal per AGENTS.md). R1(b): the judgments DDL has no uniqueness on skill_id, so name-keyed and id-keyed rows coexist and no migration is needed. comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED, gates running, NOT yet closed (I am the author; closure needs an independent verifier).

WHAT LANDED. `resolve_event_skill_reference` + `match_reference_in_members` in src/storage/ledger.rs,
wired into both `record_single_feedback` and `record_paired_correction`. Resolution happens before any
lookup keyed on the skill, so the existing-judgment check, the revision check and the write agree on one
identity. The paired path resolves BOTH references up front inside the one transaction, and the
IdenticalSkills check now also catches an id and a name that denote the same skill. An alternative that
resolves to nothing still takes the existing historically-absent path and commits zero judgments.

TWO REFINEMENTS OF MINE THAT THE CODE CORRECTED. Recording both because the bead was wrong, not the fix.

1. Refinement 2 ("do not discard the invocation name; store both") OVER-SPECIFIED. SnapshotMember already
   retains skill_id next to invocation_name, so the name a human typed stays recoverable from the very
   snapshot that resolved it. Storing it again would duplicate state that is already there. No column,
   no migration. The reasoning is in the code comment on resolve_event_skill_reference.

2. Refinement 1(b) asked whether a uniqueness constraint or foreign key on judgments.skill_id forces a

A bound on this bead's user-visible benefit, found while measuring managed-source coverage for .7.11.
It does not change the fix, which is correct; it changes what we should claim for it.

`membership_coverage == Complete` -- correctly, per SilentFinch's guard in sr-68wu, because an omitted
skill may share the name.

title: sr ledger status reports needs_migration for every freshly initialized ledger, which is fully usable
design:
## Measured, walking the P5 loop as a user

```
$ sr ledger init --json      -> status: created, schema_version: 1
$ sr ledger status --json    -> status: "needs_migration", schema_version: 1, target_version: 2
```

The same store then accepted everything the product writes: 1 ranking event, 4
ranking candidates, 2 provider attempts and 1 roster snapshot, all committed and
readable. So the store it calls "needs_migration" is the store it just created and
is using successfully.

## Why it happens

`ledger_status` computes `status = if ver == Some(LEDGER_TARGET_SCHEMA_VERSION)
{ "ready" } else { "needs_migration" }`, while `init_ledger` writes
`LEDGER_SCHEMA_VERSION`. Those constants are 1 and 2, so a fresh store can never
report ready. The only migration that exists (`v2-add-audit-log`) adds a table
nothing reads yet.

## Why it matters

The word is a instruction to the user, and it is wrong: nothing needs migrating for
the product to work. It also collapses two states a reader needs to tell apart —
"this store cannot be used until you migrate it" and "an optional later schema
exists" — which is the distinction `sr ledger migrate --apply` is gated on. A user
following the advice runs a migration to get a table with no consumer; a user
ignoring it learns to ignore status output.

PurpleFrog reported the same smell from the native-macOS side ("ledger init/status
inconsistency on eb1fbb1", mail 42380), so this is a second independent sighting.

## Shape of a fix

Report what is true about usability rather than equality with a constant. Something
like `ready` when the store is at or above `LEDGER_SCHEMA_VERSION` and writable,
with a separate, non-alarming field for an available upgrade (`upgrade_available:
2`), and `needs_migration` reserved for a store the open path actually refuses
outside `LedgerAccess::Migrate`. Whatever the shape, `sr ledger init` immediately
followed by `sr ledger status` must not tell a user their new store is unfinished.

Adjacent, much smaller: `ledger init --json` does not report the database path while
`ledger status --json` does. Worth aligning while in here.
close_reason: Fixed in 32d17b6: ledger status reports ready for fresh stores with upgrade_available, reserving needs_migration for incompatible schemas

title: A duplicate hook delivery that pays again records none of that cost: the event collides and the attempts roll back with it
design:
## Measured, with the real binary and the real hook

Dogfooded `sr hook claude` twice with the same Claude `UserPromptSubmit` payload
against the loopback TLS provider, with an initialised ledger and (accidentally,
but usefully) an unusable response cache:

- the provider served **4** requests: wide, rerank, wide, rerank;
- the ledger holds **1** ranking event and **2** attempt rows.

The second delivery's two paid requests are recorded nowhere. Both hook
invocations exited 0 and said nothing.

## Why

`derive_request_event_id` correctly returns the same id for a duplicate delivery
of the same event — that is the point of it, and idempotency is right. The event
insert then fails on the primary key, and because attempt rows are now committed
inside that same transaction (2b5b819, sr-roadmap-l1i.6.7), the rollback takes
the attempt rows with it. Before 2b5b819 nothing was lost because nothing was
recorded; the transaction is not the bug, the swallowed conflict is.

Reachability: this needs a duplicate delivery *and* a cache that cannot serve the
repeat. Both are ordinary — the store refuses a group-writable ancestor, which is
exactly the state my fixture was in, and that state is disclosed only as a
warning the hook does not print.

## The shape of the fix, and why I did not just do it

Two changes, and the first is not mine to make:

1. The event insert should recognise a duplicate rather than fail: on conflict,
   confirm the existing row carries the same identity, then keep going. A second
   delivery that really did pay twice should show one event with two attempt
   pairs, which is the truth. That changes duplicate-delivery semantics, which
   sr-7jji's owner (MistyCoyote) owns.
2. Attempt row keys need per-invocation uniqueness, not just per-owner. They are
   `{owner_event_id}:{invocation id}-att-N` and the minted invocation id is the
   literal `"rank"`, so a second delivery under the same event would collide on
   the attempt key too even after (1). The entry wall-clock millisecond reading
   is already computed for the row mapping and distinguishes invocations; folding
   it into the key is a one-line change I will make once (1) is settled.

Until both land, the honest interim reading of `provider_attempts` is: it records
the cost of first deliveries. It does not yet account for a repeat that paid.
notes:
Implemented and verified locally; pushing once the full suite reports (CopperWren).

Taken rather than left with MistyCoyote after no reply, because the rollback
coupling that turns a swallowed conflict into lost cost evidence came from my own
change, and because the fix turned out not to touch what an event means:

- the event insert is now `ON CONFLICT(event_id) DO NOTHING`, and a conflict is
  followed by reading the stored workspace, session and branch. Matching means the
  same turn arrived twice and recording continues; not matching means the id was
  reused for something else and it is still `RecordConflict`. Candidates are
  idempotent for the same reason;
- attempt row keys gained an invocation token (entry wall-clock reading plus pid),
  because the owner alone cannot separate two deliveries of one event — sharing the
  owner is precisely what they do.

Evidence: the dogfooded scenario is now a case. Two `--no-cache` deliveries of one
turn against the loopback provider must leave one event owning four rows, two wide
and two rerank with distinct keys; the store-level pair covers accumulation under
one event and refusal of an id reused for another session. Planted negative:
restoring the plain insert fails the end-to-end case with "recorded 2 attempts for
4 served requests", which is the hand-measured defect exactly.

MistyCoyote: if you would rather identity carried the invocation (passing a derived
id into `RetrySession::new` instead of the fixed word "rank"), say so and I will
move to that; I did not want two conventions, and the token is confined to the
ledger row key.
Landed b9e8b34. Full suite 114 reports / 1064 passed / 1 failed / 10 ignored; the single failure is jev_transport's shutdown-bound fragility, filed as sr-bdex and passing in isolation at the same tree.
close_reason: Fixed in b9e8b34, both halves together: duplicate deliveries are recognised rather than refused (ON CONFLICT with an identity check, so a reused id for another session is still RecordConflict), and attempt row keys carry an invocation token so a repeat that paid appends its own rows instead of colliding. Verified by the dogfooded scenario as an end-to-end case (two --no-cache deliveries: one event owning four rows) plus store-level accumulation and collision cases; planted negative reproduces the original 'recorded 2 attempts for 4 served requests'. Full suite 114/1064/1/10 with the single failure filed as sr-bdex and passing in isolation. Open preference, not a defect: MistyCoyote may prefer identity carried by the invocation id itself rather than a row-key token; I will move to that convention on request.

title: SkillRanker: complete standalone selector implementation and evidence roadmap
description:
## Goal and ownership

Deliver the complete reviewed product through P0-P9 with a useful core CLI at P4. This epic is an implementation roadmap, not the task of creating this tracker. Leave product work open until its actual acceptance evidence exists. The 15 selected improvements are integrated into component tasks; I16-I30 are deliberate dispositions, not implicit permission to build every brainstorm. Every task embeds its needed normative contract so implementers do not need the original Markdown plan.

## Product context and guardrails

SkillRanker is a standalone Rust 2024 CLI (`sr`) and pure library for next-step skill advice. Jev is the sole inference engine; fresh calls require the user's own key AND trusted network consent. Ranking never loads, executes, edits, installs or creates skills. Quill is the sole lexical engine; no active Tantivy use anywhere, no runtime `ms`, no Tokio/reqwest/ureq fallback. Keep effects bounded and secrets/private text out of diagnostics. These are implementation requirements, not statements that any product code or behavioral gate has passed.

Work on the named boundary and its focused tests. Blocking dependencies supply tested prerequisites; parent-child edges organize the roadmap and do not stand in for acceptance. Read current governing repository instructions and live dependencies before claiming work. Preserve peer changes. If a required dependency is unavailable, report the exact blocker; never replace evidence with an unmarked stub or weaken an adversarial assertion.

## Embedded contract

The following requirements define this boundary and its interactions. Implement the goal above; related behavior is supplied by the explicit prerequisite tasks.

# SkillRanker (sr) — Design and Implementation Plan

2026-09-17 · Revised after source and contract review

## Purpose and scope

SkillRanker (`sr`) is a standalone Rust CLI that recommends skills for the next step of an agent session. It captures bounded context, resolves the skills the harness can actually load, and uses TypeSafe's Jev for a broad selection followed by a more detailed rerank. Interactive output shows up to five eligible candidates; the default hook suggests at most one. Abstention is a normal result.

**TypeSafe.ai's Jev is the ranking engine, and fresh evaluations require a TypeSafe API key and authorized network access.** Local retrieval, explicit resolution, inspection, and cached results do not constitute an alternative inference backend.

The useful product is a fast, advisory selector with inspectable evidence. It does not load or execute skills, override user instructions, grant tool permissions, or decide whether an agent may continue. A failed recommendation service must not prevent the agent from working.

The initial release targets local Linux and macOS, Claude Code's `UserPromptSubmit` hook, explicit transcript input, and a versioned normalized-context format. Other harnesses can use that format immediately through an integration they control; native Codex, omp/pi, and Grok adapters require their own verified contracts before they are advertised.

**No `ms` dependency:** reuse selected code and tests from `meta_skill` inside this project. Do not invoke its CLI, link its application crate, read its private database, inherit its configuration, or write outcomes into it. Discovery, parsing, redaction, retrieval, statistics, and feedback belong to `sr`.

**Quill is the lexical search engine throughout SkillRanker.** Use `frankensearch-quill` from the user's FrankenSearch project. Do not use Tantivy for runtime search, fallback, testing, benchmarking, reference implementations, or copied code. Quill's optional upstream oracle is not enabled by this project.

Keep README.md and AGENTS.md aligned with this plan as part of P0 and whenever a public contract changes. Their main architecture has been reconciled with the standalone design; examples and detailed schemas must track subsequent corrections too. Preserve their unrelated repository, licensing, coordination, and release rules. Command examples throughout these documents are proposed interfaces, not evidence that a working binary exists.

### Evidence and limits of the starting recipe

The [TypeSafe skill-suggestion cookbook](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/skill_suggestion) reports wrong-load rates falling from 16.8% to 7.3% on 315 covered requests, and needless-load rates falling from 9.8% to 4.0% on 173 uncovered requests. Its experiment used 182 Hermes skills, a three-skill shortlist, one injected suggestion, and `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`. These are separate denominators and a particular evaluation setup, not measured results for SkillRanker.

Live multi-turn context, an eight-skill shortlist, new gate questions, personalization, and other harnesses are hypotheses to evaluate. The cookbook motivates the architecture; it does not establish our latency, cost, calibration, or effect on task success.

### Core invariants

1. Context, roster visibility, loaded-state evidence, cache entries, and feedback are bound to a workspace **and a specific session/agent branch**.
2. Explicit user skill requests and harness requirements cannot be vetoed by a probability threshold, prior, or cache. User exclusions take precedence over advisory suggestions.
3. Only locally resolved, currently loadable candidates can appear in actionable output. Provider answers cannot introduce names, paths, or commands.
4. `abstain`, `unavailable`, `explicit`, and `ranked` are different decisions. A timeout is never evidence that no skill fits.
5. Provider probabilities, local ranking scores, observed loads, and independently judged usefulness remain separate quantities.
6. Every input, subprocess, request, retry, persistence operation, and output has a bound. An HTTP-only timeout is insufficient.
7. No raw transcript or request body is persisted by default. Redaction covers all outgoing fields, including roster excerpts.
8. No skill is executed, edited, installed, or created by ranking, diagnostics, or feedback.

### Delivery discipline for these additions

I01/I05/I06/I11 build on P2–P4; I02/I09/I12/I14/I15 complete through P5; I03/I04/I13 reach hook acceptance in P6; I14 is evaluated during P7; I11's learned-policy rollback completes in P8. I07/I08/I10 remain P9 experiments. This mapping refines the existing P0–P9 dependencies rather than creating fifteen independent feature silos.

Each delivered improvement includes focused unit/property fixtures and a real CLI integration path with bounded, sanitized structured logs containing case ID, stage, policy/source versions, timings, counts, outcome, and failure kind. Never log secret matches, raw private case bodies, or credentials. Test both a successful user journey and its most consequential failure; do not settle for a help-text snapshot. Live Jev checks and real-harness checks remain distinct from offline fixture proof.

This revision was checked in five passes: overlap/user value; authority/privacy; identity/concurrency/failure; budget/statistical validity; and dependency/test completeness. The resulting corrections distinguish protected allowance state from disposable cache, trusted snoozes from learned feedback, historical alternatives from prospective library changes, and fixture results from live advice. Retain the existing core contracts and acceptance gates. A feature that increases requests, disclosure, or latency needs an explicit measured benefit at the declared budget before it can replace a default.

## Architecture and latency

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Select exact session and trusted configuration] --> B[Capture context and discover visible roster]
    B --> C[Normalize and resolve local directives before redaction and budgeting]
    C -->|explicit request| X[Locally resolved explicit result]
    C -->|local policy excludes all| N[Abstention]
    C -->|advisory candidates| Q{More than 254 eligible skills?}
    Q -->|no| D[Read matching cache and optional priors]
    Q -->|yes| QR[Bounded Quill retrieval: up to 254 matches]
    QR -->|matches| D
    QR -->|empty or failed| U[Unavailable or quiet hook fallback]
    D -->|exact hit| H[Reapply current eligibility and output policy]
    D -->|miss| BUD[Check authorized network, deadline, attempts, and provider cooldown]
    BUD -->|admitted| E[Wide Choice with none option and gate questions]
    BUD -->|refused| U
    E -->|low gate| N
    E -->|continue| RBUD[Recheck admission for rerank]
    RBUD -->|admitted| F[Rerank shortlist with none option and fit questions]
    RBUD -->|refused| U
    F --> H
    H --> I[Emit result and record bounded metadata]
    X --> I
    N --> I
    E -->|operational failure| U
    F -->|operational failure| U
    U --> I
```

Capture and discovery may overlap after the workspace/session identity is established. Wide and rerank calls are dependent; each HTTP retry repeats its stage's admission check and debit. Optional ledger reads do not authorize using another session's state. Persistence never holds a transaction across a network call.

Design targets, to be measured on named hardware, roster size, network region, and provider model:

| Path | Initial target | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact cache hit | p95 ≤100 ms | Includes validation, context tail, discovery validation, and process startup |
| Warm hook, network required | p50 ≤600 ms; p95 ≤1,500 ms | Aspirational end-to-end targets, not provider guarantees |
| Hook deadline | 3,000 ms total | Starts at process entry; reserve the final 200 ms for output/cleanup |
| Cold CLI/cass | Same configurable deadline; report stage timings | Never silently extend the timeout because discovery was slow |

The installer sets the harness timeout above `sr`'s deadline (initially 4 seconds for a 3-second run). Scheduler pauses and uninterruptible OS I/O prevent a mathematical wall-clock guarantee; slow-path tests must demonstrate bounded behavior under the supported operating conditions. If cancellation cannot bound a leaf operation, redesign that leaf before enabling it in hooks.

This deadline applies to a one-shot rank/hook invocation. A TUI/watch process has a user-controlled lifetime and starts a new bounded evaluation for each accepted refresh; it does not expire three seconds after opening. Batch evaluation has a separate overall deadline/request budget plus the per-case ranking deadline. Local maintenance commands use their own bounded batch/transaction policies, not the inference timeout.

A process launched per prompt does not inherit an earlier process's connection pool, DNS cache, or in-memory roster. Measure cold TLS and process startup separately. A persistent service is deferred until measurements justify its lifecycle and security costs.

Default installation runs once per submitted user prompt, not once per tool call. Watch mode and future tool-event hooks have separate rate limits; a forty-tool burst is not assumed to cost one request.

## Open risks with concrete resolution

| Risk or unknown | Consequence | Resolution before claiming support |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Provider total context/question limits or model alias changes | Rejected requests, invalid comparisons | P1 contract fixtures/smoke test; version/time-bound evaluation; bounded payloads |
| Native harness visibility and hook evolution | Suggestions cannot be loaded or arrive too late | Pin tested harness versions; capture real fixtures and delivery tests per adapter |
| Incomplete or injected context | Wrong recommendations or leaked data | Strict adapters, bounded redaction, authority separation, adversarial evaluation |
| Quill lexical misses/paraphrases | Relevant skill never reaches Jev | Measure candidate coverage; tune Quill analyzer/query mapping; evaluate explicit chunk experiment |
| Process startup, TLS, and roster rehash latency | Hook stalls or falls back too often | Separate stage benchmarks and cold tests; optimize measured cost before adding a daemon |
| Blocking leaf operations outlive cancellation | Timeout promise fails | Real stalled-operation tests; remove or isolate unbounded leaves |
| Observation and suggestion feedback bias | Popular skills become self-reinforcing | Separate adoption from judged usefulness; disable priors initially |
| Concurrent hooks and partial writes | Duplicate exposures or wrong attribution | Session/event keys, short transactions, crash-unknown states, bounded single-flight |
| Rare skills and sparse phase cells | Unstable learned policies | Pooled backoff, shrinkage, caps, and held-out subgroup checks |
| Redaction misses confidential prose | Unwanted disclosure | Trusted network choice, minimal-context/offline modes, payload preview |
| Large roster/ledger growth | Memory, disk, and latency regressions | Explicit caps, partial status, retention outside hook, stop optional recording at quota |

## Focused verification

Close only when required descendants and their behavioral gates are actually complete, with optional experiments honestly dispositioned and no missing required functionality concealed. Do not close this epic merely because the Beads conversion is finished.

## Evidence and logging

For each focused unit/property/integration run, keep a successful counterpart to the consequential failure case. Integration scripts must invoke real production components at the relevant filesystem, process, SQLite, TLS or CLI boundary. Structured test logs contain case ID, stage, source/policy/schema versions, timings, bounded counts, decision and failure kind; never raw private case bodies, redaction matches, credentials or reversible secrets. Save the command, exit status, exact source/lockfile/features/platform and artifact location. Lab/fixture proof, local integration, live Jev and actual harness evidence are distinct. Use RCH for expensive builds under the current compile-lane rules; DSR is the only release orchestrator. Infrastructure failure is not a pass.

## Ownership clarification

## Product improvements selected with idea-wizard

The first correctness review established what a recommendation may safely claim. This pass asks what makes the product worth using every day: finding a useful procedure, understanding a miss, controlling interruptions and expense, and fixing the underlying library or policy. The following are design priorities, not implemented features or measured improvements.

The idea-wizard pass considered 30 candidates against robustness, reliability, performance, intuitiveness, usability, ergonomics, usefulness, appeal, added value, and implementation practicality. Usefulness and practicality received the greatest weight. The top five improve the core experience without another inference provider or extra routine Jev calls. Ten supporting ideas extend existing boundaries; experiments remain gated and do not delay the core CLI.

title: P0: Contracts, scaffolding and evidence policy
description:
## Goal and ownership

Freeze common types, budgets, authority, source provenance and test contracts before parallel implementation. Documentation is not runtime proof.

## Product context and guardrails

SkillRanker is a standalone Rust 2024 CLI (`sr`) and pure library for next-step skill advice. Jev is the sole inference engine; fresh calls require the user's own key AND trusted network consent. Ranking never loads, executes, edits, installs or creates skills. Quill is the sole lexical engine; no active Tantivy use anywhere, no runtime `ms`, no Tokio/reqwest/ureq fallback. Keep effects bounded and secrets/private text out of diagnostics. These are implementation requirements, not statements that any product code or behavioral gate has passed.

Work on the named boundary and its focused tests. Blocking dependencies supply tested prerequisites; parent-child edges organize the roadmap and do not stand in for acceptance. Read current governing repository instructions and live dependencies before claiming work. Preserve peer changes. If a required dependency is unavailable, report the exact blocker; never replace evidence with an unmarked stub or weaken an adversarial assertion.

## Embedded contract

The following requirements define this boundary and its interactions. Implement the goal above; related behavior is supplied by the explicit prerequisite tasks.

## Purpose and scope

SkillRanker (`sr`) is a standalone Rust CLI that recommends skills for the next step of an agent session. It captures bounded context, resolves the skills the harness can actually load, and uses TypeSafe's Jev for a broad selection followed by a more detailed rerank. Interactive output shows up to five eligible candidates; the default hook suggests at most one. Abstention is a normal result.

**TypeSafe.ai's Jev is the ranking engine, and fresh evaluations require a TypeSafe API key and authorized network access.** Local retrieval, explicit resolution, inspection, and cached results do not constitute an alternative inference backend.

The useful product is a fast, advisory selector with inspectable evidence. It does not load or execute skills, override user instructions, grant tool permissions, or decide whether an agent may continue. A failed recommendation service must not prevent the agent from working.

The initial release targets local Linux and macOS, Claude Code's `UserPromptSubmit` hook, explicit transcript input, and a versioned normalized-context format. Other harnesses can use that format immediately through an integration they control; native Codex, omp/pi, and Grok adapters require their own verified contracts before they are advertised.

**No `ms` dependency:** reuse selected code and tests from `meta_skill` inside this project. Do not invoke its CLI, link its application crate, read its private database, inherit its configuration, or write outcomes into it. Discovery, parsing, redaction, retrieval, statistics, and feedback belong to `sr`.

**Quill is the lexical search engine throughout SkillRanker.** Use `frankensearch-quill` from the user's FrankenSearch project. Do not use Tantivy for runtime search, fallback, testing, benchmarking, reference implementations, or copied code. Quill's optional upstream oracle is not enabled by this project.

Keep README.md and AGENTS.md aligned with this plan as part of P0 and whenever a public contract changes. Their main architecture has been reconciled with the standalone design; examples and detailed schemas must track subsequent corrections too. Preserve their unrelated repository, licensing, coordination, and release rules. Command examples throughout these documents are proposed interfaces, not evidence that a working binary exists.

### Evidence and limits of the starting recipe

The [TypeSafe skill-suggestion cookbook](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/skill_suggestion) reports wrong-load rates falling from 16.8% to 7.3% on 315 covered requests, and needless-load rates falling from 9.8% to 4.0% on 173 uncovered requests. Its experiment used 182 Hermes skills, a three-skill shortlist, one injected suggestion, and `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`. These are separate denominators and a particular evaluation setup, not measured results for SkillRanker.

Live multi-turn context, an eight-skill shortlist, new gate questions, personalization, and other harnesses are hypotheses to evaluate. The cookbook motivates the architecture; it does not establish our latency, cost, calibration, or effect on task success.

### Core invariants

1. Context, roster visibility, loaded-state evidence, cache entries, and feedback are bound to a workspace **and a specific session/agent branch**.
2. Explicit user skill requests and harness requirements cannot be vetoed by a probability threshold, prior, or cache. User exclusions take precedence over advisory suggestions.
3. Only locally resolved, currently loadable candidates can appear in actionable output. Provider answers cannot introduce names, paths, or commands.
4. `abstain`, `unavailable`, `explicit`, and `ranked` are different decisions. A timeout is never evidence that no skill fits.
5. Provider probabilities, local ranking scores, observed loads, and independently judged usefulness remain separate quantities.
6. Every input, subprocess, request, retry, persistence operation, and output has a bound. An HTTP-only timeout is insufficient.
7. No raw transcript or request body is persisted by default. Redaction covers all outgoing fields, including roster excerpts.
8. No skill is executed, edited, installed, or created by ranking, diagnostics, or feedback.

## Crate layout and dependency choices

Start with one Rust package and a library exposing pure normalization, question construction, validation, eligibility, and scoring. Avoid premature workspace fragmentation.

```text
skillranker/
  Cargo.toml                 package: skillranker; binary: sr; optional tui feature
  Cargo.lock
  THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md
  src/
    main.rs                  strict CLI and mode dispatch
    lib.rs                   reusable pure pipeline components
    config.rs                provenance-aware configuration and limits
    context/
      mod.rs                 normalized records and adapter contract
      claude.rs              hook prompt overlay and native transcript decoder
      cass.rs                capability-checked optional subprocess
      normalized.rs          versioned context input
      window.rs              deterministic bounded summaries
      signals.rs             local project markers
    privacy/
      redact.rs              adapted local scanner and payload pass
      policy.rs              allowed fields, roots, endpoints, persistence
    roster/
      discover.rs            harness visibility and traversal
      frontmatter.rs         bounded metadata parser
      identity.rs            stable IDs, collisions, content versions
      retrieval.rs           bounded in-memory Quill index and candidate adapter
    jev/
      types.rs               typed request/answer schema
      transport.rs           asupersync HTTPS and bounded retries
      questions.rs           versioned wide/rerank builders
      validate.rs            response and option-set validation
      rank.rs                eligibility, abstention, blend
    ledger/
      db.rs                  schema, transactions, bounded busy behavior
      observe.rs             successful-load evidence and attribution
      feedback.rs            explicit judged labels
      priors.rs              optional centered/shrunk statistics
      calibrate.rs           held-out evaluation and candidate policy
      sampling.rs            frozen evaluation frames and inclusion probabilities
      monitor.rs             optional P8 sequential evidence and alpha accounting
    output/
      json.rs
      table.rs
      hook.rs
      tui.rs
    cache.rs                 request/decision fingerprints and TTL
    hook_install.rs          managed settings diff/apply/rollback
    diagnostics.rs           local doctor; later descriptions and gaps
  tests/
    fixtures/                sanitized synthetic/native/provider examples
    golden/                  versioned public JSON and hook output
    integration/             real filesystem, SQLite, subprocess and TLS paths
    eval/                    labeled cases, splits, scoring contracts
```

Core dependencies include asupersync (with verified TLS roots/runtime features), `frankensearch-quill` and required core types, clap, serde/serde_json, blake3, rusqlite, regex, a maintained bounded YAML parser, platform-directory handling, and appropriate error/configuration support. Pin actual versions in implementation after compatibility verification, including a compatible shared Asupersync revision. FrankenTUI is optional. No Tantivy dependency or use is permitted in any SkillRanker runtime, test, benchmark, or tooling feature; do not introduce another async runtime or an embedding service.

A line-count estimate such as “the client is 200 lines” is not an implementation contract. Transport validation, privacy, Unicode, cancellation, the Quill integration, and tests determine the necessary code.

## Implementation order and dependencies

| ID | Deliverable | Depends on | Exit evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P0 | Align companion design documentation; freeze core schemas, trust policy, resource limits, adapter/source revision manifest, initial evaluation cases, and core improvement boundaries | None | README/AGENTS design contracts reconciled; examples validate; critical unknowns named; reusable source slices and notices identified |
| P1 | Transport/runtime spike and typed response validator | P0 | Exact feature build, local TLS/timeout/cancellation proof, live bounded contract check |
| P2 | Standalone roster, metadata parsing, redaction, identities, Quill retrieval, reason codes, roster snapshots | P0 | Visibility/collision/bounds, snapshot/diff, and Quill fixtures; no `ms` dependency or active Tantivy feature/dependency |
| P3 | Claude/normalized context adapters, incremental readers, optional cass bridge, context profiles/receipts, conformance fixtures | P0 | Exact-session/prompt-timing/privacy tests; profile disclosure verified; cass/version coverage explicit |
| P4 | Pure pipeline, sentinel/gates/rerank, cache, JSON/table, dry-run, stage explanations, offline demo, configuration provenance | P1, P2, P3 | Correct finite outputs, exact invalidation, outcome-preserving explanations, useful no-key demo; API failure distinct from abstention |
| P5 | Minimal ledger, case capture/replay/comparison, corrective feedback, value reports, evaluation with sampling and perturbation suites | P4 | Idempotent observations, faithful non-actionable replay, partial-label handling, validated denominators, labeled benchmark report |
| P6 | Claude shadow wrapper, installer/rollback, request allowance/circuit breaker, scoped snoozes, operational deadline tests | P4, P5 | Real supported harness and concurrent-process admission; quiet abstentions/failures; measured timings and setup flow |
| P7 | Advisory rollout and manual feedback/statistics | P6 | Predeclared quality and latency gates; usefulness/interruption/usage report; local rollback switch |
| P8 | Calibration and explicit policy rollback, optional priors, budgeted sequential monitoring | P5, P7 | Independent labels, held-out improvement, valid evidence/alpha accounting, conflict-safe reversible policy |
| P9 | Description/gap analysis and overlays, Quill passage/query-view experiments, TUI, further adapters, experimental chunking | P7; relevant P8 outputs only if used | Separate feature-specific gates and equal-budget comparisons; no unmeasured change to defaults |

P1–P3 are independent implementation tracks; the table describes dependencies, not permission to bypass validation. Core CLI work is useful at P4. Hook rollout waits for minimal observability and tests; adaptive learning stays later.

P0 need not finalize P9 experimental interfaces. Budget guards and snoozes first ship through P6, replay through P5, and learned-policy rollback through P8; a core-only build reports those later capabilities as unavailable rather than exposing unfinished command paths.

Do not hold the usable CLI hostage to TUI, corpus mining, a second database engine, or generalized harness support. Conversely, privacy, bounded execution, abstention, and session identity are core behavior, not post-launch hardening.

## Focused verification

The executable P0 acceptance gate and all required children carry actual revision-bound evidence. Parent completion never replaces individual tests or advertises unavailable commands.

## Evidence and logging

For each focused unit/property/integration run, keep a successful counterpart to the consequential failure case. Integration scripts must invoke real production components at the relevant filesystem, process, SQLite, TLS or CLI boundary. Structured test logs contain case ID, stage, source/policy/schema versions, timings, bounded counts, decision and failure kind; never raw private case bodies, redaction matches, credentials or reversible secrets. Save the command, exit status, exact source/lockfile/features/platform and artifact location. Lab/fixture proof, local integration, live Jev and actual harness evidence are distinct. Use RCH for expensive builds under the current compile-lane rules; DSR is the only release orchestrator. Infrastructure failure is not a pass.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Deliver the scoped behavior and every applicable embedded invariant, with no undocumented authority, persistence or inference effects.
- [ ] The executable P0 acceptance gate and all required children carry actual revision-bound evidence. Parent completion never replaces individual tests or advertises unavailable commands.
- [ ] Attach exact revision-bound verification commands/results and sanitized artifacts; distinguish not-run/blocked from passed and preserve honest success cases.
- [ ] Update affected public schemas, capabilities and examples when the implemented boundary changes; do not advertise later features early.
notes: Implementation has started in bv-recommended dependency order. The complete 186-bead acceptance/TODO inventory is maintained in live br and a recovery snapshot at /data/tmp/skillranker-execution-m0ip1wu3/TODO.md. First batch: dependency qualification, frozen evaluation policy, Rust bootstrap, identity/provenance and resource/deadline contracts. Each child closes only with its own scoped evidence; no parent acceptance or product-ranking capability is implied.
close_reason: All 16 P0 children (.1.1 through .1.16) are closed. P0 contracts, scaffolding, and evidence policy accepted and verified in docs/p0-acceptance.md and docs/verification-p0-acceptance.json.

title: Reconcile public contracts and staged capabilities
description:
## Goal and ownership

Synchronize README, AGENTS, examples and capability schema with the accepted contracts; distinguish design-only, P4 core, P5 evaluation, P6 shadow, P7 advisory, P8 learning and P9 experiments. Preserve contribution and release rules.

## Product context and guardrails

SkillRanker is a standalone Rust 2024 CLI (`sr`) and pure library for next-step skill advice. Jev is the sole inference engine; fresh calls require the user's own key AND trusted network consent. Ranking never loads, executes, edits, installs or creates skills. Quill is the sole lexical engine; no active Tantivy use anywhere, no runtime `ms`, no Tokio/reqwest/ureq fallback. Keep effects bounded and secrets/private text out of diagnostics. These are implementation requirements, not statements that any product code or behavioral gate has passed.

Work on the named boundary and its focused tests. Blocking dependencies supply tested prerequisites; parent-child edges organize the roadmap and do not stand in for acceptance. Read current governing repository instructions and live dependencies before claiming work. Preserve peer changes. If a required dependency is unavailable, report the exact blocker; never replace evidence with an unmarked stub or weaken an adversarial assertion.

## Embedded contract

The following requirements define this boundary and its interactions. Implement the goal above; related behavior is supplied by the explicit prerequisite tasks.

## Purpose and scope

SkillRanker (`sr`) is a standalone Rust CLI that recommends skills for the next step of an agent session. It captures bounded context, resolves the skills the harness can actually load, and uses TypeSafe's Jev for a broad selection followed by a more detailed rerank. Interactive output shows up to five eligible candidates; the default hook suggests at most one. Abstention is a normal result.

**TypeSafe.ai's Jev is the ranking engine, and fresh evaluations require a TypeSafe API key and authorized network access.** Local retrieval, explicit resolution, inspection, and cached results do not constitute an alternative inference backend.

The useful product is a fast, advisory selector with inspectable evidence. It does not load or execute skills, override user instructions, grant tool permissions, or decide whether an agent may continue. A failed recommendation service must not prevent the agent from working.

The initial release targets local Linux and macOS, Claude Code's `UserPromptSubmit` hook, explicit transcript input, and a versioned normalized-context format. Other harnesses can use that format immediately through an integration they control; native Codex, omp/pi, and Grok adapters require their own verified contracts before they are advertised.

**No `ms` dependency:** reuse selected code and tests from `meta_skill` inside this project. Do not invoke its CLI, link its application crate, read its private database, inherit its configuration, or write outcomes into it. Discovery, parsing, redaction, retrieval, statistics, and feedback belong to `sr`.

**Quill is the lexical search engine throughout SkillRanker.** Use `frankensearch-quill` from the user's FrankenSearch project. Do not use Tantivy for runtime search, fallback, testing, benchmarking, reference implementations, or copied code. Quill's optional upstream oracle is not enabled by this project.

Keep README.md and AGENTS.md aligned with this plan as part of P0 and whenever a public contract changes. Their main architecture has been reconciled with the standalone design; examples and detailed schemas must track subsequent corrections too. Preserve their unrelated repository, licensing, coordination, and release rules. Command examples throughout these documents are proposed interfaces, not evidence that a working binary exists.

### Evidence and limits of the starting recipe

The [TypeSafe skill-suggestion cookbook](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/skill_suggestion) reports wrong-load rates falling from 16.8% to 7.3% on 315 covered requests, and needless-load rates falling from 9.8% to 4.0% on 173 uncovered requests. Its experiment used 182 Hermes skills, a three-skill shortlist, one injected suggestion, and `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`. These are separate denominators and a particular evaluation setup, not measured results for SkillRanker.

Live multi-turn context, an eight-skill shortlist, new gate questions, personalization, and other harnesses are hypotheses to evaluate. The cookbook motivates the architecture; it does not establish our latency, cost, calibration, or effect on task success.

### Core invariants

1. Context, roster visibility, loaded-state evidence, cache entries, and feedback are bound to a workspace **and a specific session/agent branch**.
2. Explicit user skill requests and harness requirements cannot be vetoed by a probability threshold, prior, or cache. User exclusions take precedence over advisory suggestions.
3. Only locally resolved, currently loadable candidates can appear in actionable output. Provider answers cannot introduce names, paths, or commands.
4. `abstain`, `unavailable`, `explicit`, and `ranked` are different decisions. A timeout is never evidence that no skill fits.
5. Provider probabilities, local ranking scores, observed loads, and independently judged usefulness remain separate quantities.
6. Every input, subprocess, request, retry, persistence operation, and output has a bound. An HTTP-only timeout is insufficient.
7. No raw transcript or request body is persisted by default. Redaction covers all outgoing fields, including roster excerpts.
8. No skill is executed, edited, installed, or created by ranking, diagnostics, or feedback.

### Commands and release stages

| Command | Purpose | Earliest gated phase |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sr` / `sr rank` | Rank from explicit context/transcript or selected session | P4 |
| `sr hook claude` | Harness protocol wrapper; bounded stdin and shadow output | P6; advisory rollout P7 |
| `sr roster --json` | Inspect visibility, precedence, records, and exclusions | P2 |
| `sr roster --snapshot FILE` / `sr roster --diff FILE` | Explicit bounded manifest export or local drift comparison | P2 |
| `sr doctor --json` | Local configuration/adapter/transport readiness checks | P4 |
| `sr doctor --config` | Explain effective non-secret values and their trusted sources | P4 |
| `sr demo --case NAME` | Offline, non-actionable synthetic/recorded fixture demonstration | P4 |
| `sr capabilities --json` | Schema versions, compiled features, supported adapters/events, limits, exit codes | P4 |
| `sr install-hook claude` / `sr uninstall-hook claude` | Preview settings change; `--apply` writes | P6 |
| `sr stats --since 7d --by-skill` | Observation and operational metrics | P5 |
| `sr observe --transcript FILE --harness NAME` | Reconcile native loads; cass/normalized alternatives retain ranking's source semantics | P5 |
| `sr feedback EVENT --skill ID --verdict VERDICT` | Store explicit usefulness judgment | P5 |
| `sr feedback EVENT --skill ID --instead ID` | Record a partial explicit correction without labeling all other skills | P5 |
| `sr snooze EVENT --skill ID --for DURATION` | Preview temporary scoped advisory control; `--apply` writes | P6 |
| `sr budget` | Inspect local request allowance; bounded setup/change preview and `--apply` | P6 |
| `sr replay FILE` | Offline non-actionable replay; optional compatible local policy comparison | P5 |
| `sr eval --dataset FILE` | Offline replay by default; live runs require `--online`, authorization, and a request cap | P5 |
| `sr calibrate --evaluation FILE` | Report proposed thresholds; `--apply` installs scoped config | P8 |
| `sr calibrate --rollback REVISION` | Preview restoring only managed policy fields; `--apply` writes | P8 |
| `sr ledger init` / `sr ledger migrate` | Explicit initialization; migration preview and `--apply` | P5 |
| `sr ledger prune` / `sr ledger clear` | Preview retention operation; `--apply` mutates | P5 |
| `sr tui` | Inline viewer and watch mode | P9 |
| `sr doctor --descriptions` / `sr gaps` | Description/coverage diagnostics | P9 |

Shared ranking controls: `--messages 12`, `--budget-chars 12000`, `--top 5`, `--shortlist 8`, `--gate 0.30`, `--fits 0.30`, `--timeout-ms 3000`, `--roster FILE`, repeatable `--require-skill ID`, `--no-tools`, `--no-cache`, `--no-ledger`, `--no-persist`, `--offline`, `--allow-network`, and `--explain`. Mode-specific flags reject incompatible combinations.

I01/I02/I06 add `--why-not ID` (with `--explain`), CLI-only `--save-case FILE`, and `--context-profile standard|minimal`. Replay's `--policy`/`--compare-policy` accept only the supported local policy schema, never executable code or credential/routing settings. Feedback verdict and replacement modes are mutually exclusive. Snooze requires exactly one skill/all/clear mode with a verified event scope; duration is required for skill/all and forbidden for clear. Capabilities advertise each interface only when its implementation and relevant phase gate exist.

`sr rank --dry-run` builds the wide payload without calling the API. When explicit resolution or local eligibility ends the pipeline before inference, report that decision and that no provider request would be made. To preview stage 2, require `--shortlist-ids ...` or an explicit validated recorded wide response; a network-free command cannot know an unevaluated model's top eight. It performs no observation reconciliation or persistent writes.

Use strict clap parsing with documented aliases only. Do not silently normalize arbitrary misspellings, case, or single-dash flags: errors in hooks and privacy flags must be detectable.

Configuration precedence for ordinary values: built-in defaults → trusted user config → allowlisted project config → recognized `SR_*` environment → CLI flags. Resolve the project config at the workspace root, not by whichever nested directory happened to invoke the hook. Security-sensitive values exclude the project layer.

Use platform configuration directories; Linux fallback `~/.config/sr/config.toml`. `SR_MODEL` overrides the model. `TYPESAFE_ENDPOINT` is recognized only under the trusted base-origin rules. After bounded configuration reads, validate unknown/duplicate keys, bounds, NaN/infinity, and conflicts before session discovery, networking, or persistent mutations; do not silently ignore misspelled privacy settings. Known settings forbidden in project configuration are reported as configuration errors, not silently accepted. `doctor --config` may display their blocked status without producing a valid effective runtime policy.

## Implementation order and dependencies

| ID | Deliverable | Depends on | Exit evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P0 | Align companion design documentation; freeze core schemas, trust policy, resource limits, adapter/source revision manifest, initial evaluation cases, and core improvement boundaries | None | README/AGENTS design contracts reconciled; examples validate; critical unknowns named; reusable source slices and notices identified |
| P1 | Transport/runtime spike and typed response validator | P0 | Exact feature build, local TLS/timeout/cancellation proof, live bounded contract check |
| P2 | Standalone roster, metadata parsing, redaction, identities, Quill retrieval, reason codes, roster snapshots | P0 | Visibility/collision/bounds, snapshot/diff, and Quill fixtures; no `ms` dependency or active Tantivy feature/dependency |
| P3 | Claude/normalized context adapters, incremental readers, optional cass bridge, context profiles/receipts, conformance fixtures | P0 | Exact-session/prompt-timing/privacy tests; profile disclosure verified; cass/version coverage explicit |
| P4 | Pure pipeline, sentinel/gates/rerank, cache, JSON/table, dry-run, stage explanations, offline demo, configuration provenance | P1, P2, P3 | Correct finite outputs, exact invalidation, outcome-preserving explanations, useful no-key demo; API failure distinct from abstention |
| P5 | Minimal ledger, case capture/replay/comparison, corrective feedback, value reports, evaluation with sampling and perturbation suites | P4 | Idempotent observations, faithful non-actionable replay, partial-label handling, validated denominators, labeled benchmark report |
| P6 | Claude shadow wrapper, installer/rollback, request allowance/circuit breaker, scoped snoozes, operational deadline tests | P4, P5 | Real supported harness and concurrent-process admission; quiet abstentions/failures; measured timings and setup flow |
| P7 | Advisory rollout and manual feedback/statistics | P6 | Predeclared quality and latency gates; usefulness/interruption/usage report; local rollback switch |
| P8 | Calibration and explicit policy rollback, optional priors, budgeted sequential monitoring | P5, P7 | Independent labels, held-out improvement, valid evidence/alpha accounting, conflict-safe reversible policy |
| P9 | Description/gap analysis and overlays, Quill passage/query-view experiments, TUI, further adapters, experimental chunking | P7; relevant P8 outputs only if used | Separate feature-specific gates and equal-budget comparisons; no unmeasured change to defaults |

P1–P3 are independent implementation tracks; the table describes dependencies, not permission to bypass validation. Core CLI work is useful at P4. Hook rollout waits for minimal observability and tests; adaptive learning stays later.

P0 need not finalize P9 experimental interfaces. Budget guards and snoozes first ship through P6, replay through P5, and learned-policy rollback through P8; a core-only build reports those later capabilities as unavailable rather than exposing unfinished command paths.

Do not hold the usable CLI hostage to TUI, corpus mining, a second database engine, or generalized harness support. Conversely, privacy, bounded execution, abstention, and session identity are core behavior, not post-launch hardening.

## Focused verification

Validate JSON/TOML/shell examples, anchors and license; confirm own TypeSafe key/network requirement and no ms/Tantivy promises; docs cannot advertise unfinished commands as implemented.

## Evidence and logging

For each focused unit/property/integration run, keep a successful counterpart to the consequential failure case. Integration scripts must invoke real production components at the relevant filesystem, process, SQLite, TLS or CLI boundary. Structured test logs contain case ID, stage, source/policy/schema versions, timings, bounded counts, decision and failure kind; never raw private case bodies, redaction matches, credentials or reversible secrets. Save the command, exit status, exact source/lockfile/features/platform and artifact location. Lab/fixture proof, local integration, live Jev and actual harness evidence are distinct. Use RCH for expensive builds under the current compile-lane rules; DSR is the only release orchestrator. Infrastructure failure is not a pass.

## Open risks with concrete resolution

| Risk or unknown | Consequence | Resolution before claiming support |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Provider total context/question limits or model alias changes | Rejected requests, invalid comparisons | P1 contract fixtures/smoke test; version/time-bound evaluation; bounded payloads |
| Native harness visibility and hook evolution | Suggestions cannot be loaded or arrive too late | Pin tested harness versions; capture real fixtures and delivery tests per adapter |

title: Prove the test driver rejects false passes and unsafe diagnostic logs
description:
## Goal and ownership

Verify that the test driver can detect failures before relying on it to certify SkillRanker. This owns the independent runner/evidence self-test, not future product behavior. Keep the source pipeline, Jev-only ranking, Quill-only retrieval, no runtime ms dependency and all privacy/authority rules intact.

## Required scenarios

Implement `scripts/e2e/run.sh --suite runner-contract --artifacts DIR` using tiny purpose-built child fixtures plus the real report validator. A passing child and expected refusal are successful twins. Inject a failing command hidden before a pipe/tee, nonzero child exit, signal, hang, malformed/truncated event record, duplicate/missing case ID, empty test selection, expected fault never reached, incompatible binary/schema identity and a failed attempt followed by a passing retry. Every case must be classified correctly and the outer runner must never turn these into an overall passed required suite. Verify report cardinalities and exactly one terminal state per started case, while a forcibly interrupted run remains visibly incomplete.

Check private artifact permissions and hostile log strings: planted credential, raw provider error, terminal escape, newline injection, secret-valued argument and inherited environment. The report must retain useful assertion/stage/status metadata while removing unsafe values; inspect stdout, stderr, events and summary. Exhaust a declared artifact/pipe budget and prove that truncation cannot hide failure. Use per-case/global deadlines and kill/reap owned children, leave operator state untouched, and retain failures for diagnosis.

Validate the mapping schema for unit/property/e2e owner, phase, platform/features, case and assertion IDs. P0 rows for future product tests are planned, never fake passed results. Later phase gates require their complete real cases. Default tests deny external network; actual-provider evidence needs separately declared consent and request limits.

## Evidence and logging

Use independent expected classifications rather than the classifier under test to generate its own oracle. Retain versioned case-level NDJSON, final count reconciliation, rerun instructions, source/fixture/runner hashes, elapsed times and child exit/signal. Publish a complete pass only after the adversarial self-test shows the runner fails when it should. These checks prove the harness, not SkillRanker correctness or live integrations.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Run the named runner-contract suite with passing and deliberately failing children, all required failure classes, and exact independent expected classifications.
- [ ] Prove zero tests, skipped prerequisites, missing records, pipeline failures, unreached faults and pass-after-failure retries cannot certify a complete suite.
- [ ] Inspect all artifacts and diagnostic channels for planted secrets and controls while retaining useful bounded failure evidence.
- [ ] Validate future-phase coverage rows without inventing product execution; record exact source, schema, fixture and platform evidence.
prerequisites:
Blocking prerequisites:
- sr-roadmap-l1i.1.9: Build sanitized test and evidence scaffolding. Consume its accepted boundary.

title: Implement bounded process and evidence engine for the P0 test runner
description:
Implement the schema-independent process/evidence engine extracted from sr-roadmap-l1i.1.9 so work can proceed while product output schema .1.3 is still in progress. This is concrete required P0 scaffolding, not product ranking or release acceptance.

Deliver scripts/e2e/run.sh and Python stdlib runner/validator modules, a versioned evidence event/summary schema, isolated private run directories, a strict child protocol, bounded pipes/artifacts/case and aggregate deadlines, process-group termination/reaping, fixed allowlisted diagnostics, exact executable/source/lockfile/runner/fixture hashes, and a default-deny external-network boundary that reports unsupported enforcement as blocked. Never inherit provider credentials, proxy/routing configuration or operator state. No arbitrary live suite execution; provider and actual-harness evidence remain blocked until separate trusted consent and frozen budgets exist.

The runner accepts a checked-in suite manifest with unique safe case/step/assertion IDs and explicit expected child behavior. Nonzero exits, signals, timeouts, malformed/missing/duplicate event records, zero cases, incomplete selection, unreached required faults, revision/schema mismatches and a failed attempt followed by a pass cannot produce a passed complete suite. An expected refusal passes only when the precise independent expected exit/status/assertions and absence-of-effects checks agree. Child stdout/stderr are never copied into diagnostics; reports preserve only allowlisted bounded metadata. Emit private events.jsonl and summary.json with exact count reconciliation and one terminal result per started case. A run interrupted before finalization is visibly incomplete. Retain failed evidence and never silently retry away a failure.

Focused self-tests use real temporary files and owned subprocesses, including planted secret/control text, pipe exhaustion and a passing counterpart. They prove runner mechanics only, not Jev, native harness, SQLite, TLS, ranking or future product behavior. Compilation remains separately recorded RCH work and releases remain DSR-only.

The original .1.9 retains full contract-matrix ownership and integration with accepted .1.3 output schemas, and .1.12 retains the independent adversarial certification suite. This task does not remove either acceptance gate. No existing features or tests are dropped.
