title: One stray file in a skills root disables all ranking (real-machine dogfood)
description:
## Observed by installing the real binary and using it (release build of 221494f, ~/.local/bin/sr)

On an ordinary Claude Code machine, `sr rank` cannot rank anything. My real ~/.claude/skills holds 209 entries: 204 valid skill directories plus a few stray files that are not skills at all (two COMPREHENSIVE_BACKGROUND_RESEARCH_*.md notes, a PARENT_DIR_CONTAINS_GIT_REPO_FOR_THIS.info marker, and one skill whose SKILL.md is 508 KB). Every rank invocation returns exit 5:

  {"kind":"empty-roster","message":"No eligible skills found in roster","hint":"Check skill directory paths or frontmatter syntax."}

sr doctor reports skills 204, unverified 204, advisory 0, record_causes {unreadable: 1, unsupported-layout: 24}. Inspection sees the skills; ranking refuses all of them. Even `sr rank --require-skill beads-br` fails with unresolved-explicit for a skill that plainly exists.

## Mechanism

src/roster/resolution.rs:516-525 sets discovery_withhold = true when ANY discovery diagnostic is not RootMissing or SourceNotEnumerated, and then downgrades EVERY entry to Visibility::Unverified. src/pipeline.rs:1036 admits only bindings matching Visibility::Verified{..}, so initial_advisory is empty and pipeline.rs:1045 returns EmptyRoster. One unrecognized file therefore disables the whole product, globally, for every workspace that user opens.

The adjacent branch is already correct: when withheld_names is non-empty it downgrades only the specific invocation names at risk. A stray .md or .info file cannot claim any invocation name, so it should take that narrow path (or be ignored outright), not the global one.

## Proof, both directions

Negative: in a clean scratch workspace with two well-formed project skills, rank still returns empty-roster, because HOME still holds the stray files (the withhold is global, not per-root).
Positive: with HOME pointed at a directory containing exactly one well-formed skill, the same command ranks correctly and builds a full provider request. With a mirror HOME containing the 204 valid skills and the stray files excluded, `sr rank` over my real 44 MB session transcript returned decision=ranked in 1.8 s with 204 eligible, suggesting reality-check-for-project (fits 0.73). So the only thing standing between a real user and a working product is the stray files.

## Acceptance

Reject or ignore an unrecognized file without withholding authority from unrelated skills; keep the narrow per-name withholding for candidates that could actually claim a name; real-filesystem regressions covering a skills root that mixes valid skills with a README, a dotfile, a non-skill directory and an oversized SKILL.md, asserting the valid skills still rank. The current hint ("Check skill directory paths or frontmatter syntax") is also misleading and should name the actual excluded paths.

title: One oversized transcript record fails the Claude overlay: 4/80 real sessions withhold on a large tool result
description: Found by AzureJaguar 2026-09-22 in a sandboxed sr hook claude replay of the 80 most recent real transcripts: 4 fail 'existing transcript file is malformed: transcript record exceeds byte limit'. Every oversized record (279-555 KiB) is a mid-chain record with children: tool_result records (content duplicated in message and toolUseResult), or one user message with two images. The overlay maps SkipKind::Oversize to MalformedTranscript, so one large tool output anywhere in the 2 MiB tail withholds every later prompt in that session. An oversized record is over the parse limit, not malformed. Fix: read only its lineage identity (type/uuid/parentUuid/sessionId/isSidechain) with a bounded identity-only deserializer that skips other values without building them; keep it as a content-free placeholder like other harness records; mark the context Partial. Keep duplicate identity keys, session mismatch and genuine corruption fatal.

title: Cache can pair an old wide answer with a rerank from a different evaluation
description: Reported by the 2026-09-23 review (cache cluster). lookup_pair (src/pipeline.rs ~2213-2245) reads each stage separately. record_response_inner uses INSERT OR REPLACE per stage, and publish_evaluation (src/storage/publication.rs), which replaces the namespace and checks rerank.received_at >= wide.received_at, is only called by a test. Every entry is stored with model_revision None, so it counts as an unversioned alias, and AGENTS.md forbids mixing an old wide answer with a fresh rerank there. Timeline: run A caches W1 and R1 under rerank fingerprint X. Run B (a different wide set, same shortlist) replaces R1 with R2 under X. A rerun of A is then served W1 with R2.
close_reason: 4fd3b25: rerank cache keys now include the fingerprint of the wide request whose answer produced the shortlist (RequestFingerprintInput.paired_wide, hashed with a presence tag). A rerank recorded for another evaluation cannot complete a cached wide answer: it is a miss, so a mixed pair under an unversioned alias is impossible by construction. Test cache_fingerprint::a_rerank_key_is_bound_to_the_wide_answer_that_produced_its_shortlist. RCH full suite 1362/1/10; the one failure was an unrelated starvation case fixed in 2abda54. Clippy clean.

title: Preserve exact skill names in prompt directives
description: Observed parser lowercases the entire natural-language directive and splits on every period before extracting target. This silently redirects CaseSkill to caseskill and truncates Review.Tools to review. Preserve original target bytes while matching directive vocabulary case-insensitively; distinguish sentence punctuation from internal dots. Prove direct parser and actual-file resolver success for mixed-case/dotted names, lowercase decoy does not replace requested skill, negative directives preserve exact identity, sentence-separated directives and existing quote/code tests unchanged. No pipeline edits or broad natural-language grammar expansion.
close_reason: Exact target case and internal dots preserved; lowercase decoy regression and fresh actual-file resolution pass.
